subject: The mountline.dev homepage, before and after its September 2026 rebuild

before.description: the homepage as it was live before the rebuild

after.description: the rebuilt homepage, as a local production build

environment.network: Both builds served locally by `next start`. Lighthouse simulates a slow 4G connection and a 4× slower processor.

checks.label: The offer is on the first screen
checks.means: The headline and a way to start a project are visible without scrolling.

checks.label: One tap reaches the form
checks.means: “Talk about your project” lands on the form’s first field.

checks.label: Asking about a service fills it in
checks.means: “Ask about Capture” opens the form with Photo and video already chosen.

checks.label: The same for the receptionist
checks.means: “Ask about the receptionist” opens the form with it already chosen.

checks.label: Mistakes are explained
checks.means: Sending an empty form lists what’s missing and moves to the first problem.

checks.label: Nothing typed is lost
checks.means: After a mistake, everything already typed is still there.

checks.label: The server checks every message
checks.means: A controlled test submission reaches the server, is checked, and is refused on purpose, so nothing is saved.

checks.label: The example starts at once
checks.means: Pressing play on the receptionist example starts it immediately.

checks.label: The outcome is always in reach
checks.means: The example’s finished message can be read without waiting for the end.

checks.label: The real demo line is next to it
checks.means: The phone number for the live demo line is shown with the example.

checks.label: Keyboard users can skip ahead
checks.means: The first key press offers a jump straight to the content.

checks.label: You can always see where you are
checks.means: Every stop on the keyboard path, down to the form, is visibly highlighted.

checks.label: Automated accessibility scan
checks.means: axe-core finds no WCAG A/AA rule failures on the page.

checks.label: Nothing spills off the side
checks.means: No sideways scrolling at 360, 390, 768, 1024, 1440, or 1920 pixels wide.

checks.label: The browser demo never fakes a call
checks.means: With the microphone blocked, or the browser demo switched off, it says so and offers the phone line instead.

accessibility.tool: axe-core 4.13.0, WCAG 2.2 A and AA rules

performance.profile: Mobile preset, runs of both builds interleaved

unitTests.covers: Inquiry validation, saving through the real database function in an in-process Postgres, duplicate and rate-limit protection, email jobs, public-claim rules, and the receptionist setup and browser-demo server code.

findings.title: A link that missed on phones
findings.found: A mid-build test caught “Talk about your project” landing on the word-built mark on phones, with the form below the screen.
findings.fix: The form now comes right after the heading.
findings.source: The “One tap reaches the form” check, mid-build run and final run

findings.title: Content that moved while scrolling
findings.found: A mid-build test caught content shifting as a desktop screen scrolled past this scene, because the frame resized itself to become a phone. The old homepage had none.
findings.fix: Now it changes shape without moving anything.
findings.source: Scripted scroll through the whole page with a 4× slower processor, mid-build run and final run

findings.title: Fonts nobody saw
findings.found: The old homepage loaded 411 KB of fonts, including a serif only our team dashboard uses.
findings.fix: Now that one loads only there.
findings.source: Median of the Lighthouse mobile runs

findings.title: Text too faint to read
findings.found: A scan found 10 bits of text too faint to read, mostly faded questions in the old scrolling list.
findings.fix: Every line now clears the minimum.
findings.source: axe-core color-contrast rule, desktop and phone

notTested: Conversations with the live AI receptionist. No test calls were approved for this build, so its answers are not scored here.
A real browser call to the demo. With placeholder settings, its error paths were exercised (6 of 6 behaved as designed), but no real call was made because the provider keys aren’t set up yet.
Email delivery to a real inbox. A provider accepting an email doesn’t prove it arrived.
Physical phones. Phone results come from an emulated phone screen in desktop Chrome.
limits: Lab measurements from one computer on one day. Your customers’ phones and connections will differ.
Automated accessibility scans catch some problems, not all of them.
These are recorded results, not a test running in your browser now.
